records.public_safe_text: unit 1 is a motorist [roadway] 2 of the 10400 block of nacogdoches approaching the intersection of nacogdoches and town lake. unit 2 is a pedestrian and was walking northeast on the sidewalk adjacent to the southwest-bound lanes of nacogdoches. unit 2 was also approaching the intersection of nacogdoches and town lake. unit 2 was facing a ""walk"" pedestrian crosswalk signal indicating that unit 2 had the lawful right of way to proceed across town lake on the marked crosswalk. unit 1 was facing a solid green traffic signal indicating that unit 1 had the lawful right of way to proceed straight down nacogdoches across town lake, but was still required to yield to pedestrian traffic if making a right-hand turn on town lake. unit 1 made a right-hand turn onto town lake while unit 2 was occupying the crosswalk. as unit 1 turned from southwest nacogdoches to northwest nacogdoches unit 1 was facing directly west in the middle of the turn, staring straight into the setting sun. the sun obscured unit 1's vision to an extent that unit 1 did not see unit 2 crossing town lake via the crosswalk. unit 1 crashed into unit 2 at a low speed. unit 1 immediately stopped and rendered aid to unit 2. unit 1 had no damage. unit 2 had minor/superficial scrapes that were evaluated at the scene by ems. ems determined that unit 2's injuries did not require immediate medical attention and unit 2 was not transported. there are no criminal charges associated with this crash.

records.public_safe_text: on october 22nd, 2021, i, officer dobbs 9060, responded to a crash hs call located at 5319 n ih 35 svrd nb. the call text stated that a pedestrian had been hit by a vehicle and was laying in the roadway. upon arrival i observed the victim to be laying in the middle of the roadway on her side. the victim was laying on her left side and blood was coming from her nose, mouth, and head. i checked for a pulse and i felt a faint pulse on the victim. ems and arrived on immediately transported the victim to [medical facility] where she was later pronounced deceased at 2253. i spoke with a witness who did not see the actual crash but saw a possible suspect vehicle just moments before. [person] stated that just before the incident he was leaving the best buy located at [roadway]. he stated that as he was at the light about to [roadway] a black sedan, possible nissan, driving at a very high rate of speed ran the red light [roadway] almost causing a collision with his vehicle. after the vehicle did this he then [roadway] and began driving nb. moments later after passing under the [roadway] bridge, mason stated that he observed a bunch of debris that looked to be falling from the sky and just settling on the ground. that is when he noticed that there was a body on the ground and came to a stop to block for traffic. when he approached the body he stated that there was no blood on the ground and only the unresponsive victim. he began to call for emergency services and when he did this he stated that the victim began to start bleeding excessively. shortly after pd arrived.
records.redacted_narrative: on october 22nd, 2021, i, officer dobbs 9060, responded to a crash hs call located at 5319 n ih 35 svrd nb. the call text stated that a pedestrian had been hit by a vehicle and was laying in the roadway. upon arrival i observed the victim to be laying in the middle of the roadway on her side. the victim was laying on her left side and blood was coming from her nose, mouth, and head. i checked for a pulse and i felt a faint pulse on the victim. ems and arrived on immediately transported the victim to [medical facility] where she was later pronounced deceased at 2253. i spoke with a witness who did not see the actual crash but saw a possible suspect vehicle just moments before. [person] stated that just before the incident he was leaving the best buy located at [roadway]. he stated that as he was at the light about to [roadway] a black sedan, possible nissan, driving at a very high rate of speed ran the red light [roadway] almost causing a collision with his vehicle. after the vehicle did this he then [roadway] and began driving nb. moments later after passing under the [roadway] bridge, mason stated that he observed a bunch of debris that looked to be falling from the sky and just settling on the ground. that is when he noticed that there was a body on the ground and came to a stop to block for traffic. when he approached the body he stated that there was no blood on the ground and only the unresponsive victim. he began to call for emergency services and when he did this he stated that the victim began to start bleeding excessively. shortly after pd arrived.

records.deidentified_narrative: on december 31, 2021 at approximately 2000 hours i, deputy chief n. stringer of the reno police department, was dispatched to a vehicle vs. pedestrian crash in the 1600 block of arvel circle in reno, parker county, texas. upon arrival i saw a man, later identified as keith thomas freeman, laying approximately 5-7 feet off the roadway in the grass. freeman was in obvious shock and appeared to be in a great deal of pain. it was immediately apparent both of freemans legs were broken. i also saw a silver dodge ram bearing texas license plate [identifier] sitting approximately 10 feet from freeman. there was a female in the drivers seat, later identified as misty dawn lindley w/f [date]. she was stating she didnt mean to hit freeman as i approached the drivers side of the vehicle. i immediately saw there were long tire marks [roadway] leading up to the point of impact. lieutenant a. nalley also told me he had responded to a rolling domestic with these two subjects earlier in the day. those factors led me to believe this may have been an assault. i removed lindley from the drivers seat and placed her into handcuffs, double locked, behind her back. i explained she was being detained and i placed her into the back seat of sergeant e. gonzalezs car. i attempted to ask freeman what happened but he was in a state of shock that he was unable to answer any of my questions. after paramedics removed freeman from the scene, officers began the scene investigation. it was immediately apparent lindley had run over freeman and then reversed back over him after striking him. once the front passenger side of the truck made contact with freeman, he fell and the truck rolled over him with the passenger side front tire. lindley then placed the vehicle in reverse and backed up causing the passenger side front tire to roll over freeman a second time before freemans body and the truck [roadway] where officers discovered them upon arrival. this was evidenced by tire marks attached to this report. there were also fresh scratches on the front bumper on the passenger side of the truck which matched freemans watch as he tried to grab the bumper in attempt to prevent himself from going underneath the truck. i also saw a section of tire marks just behind the drivers side rear tire which evidenced lindley accelerating rapidly right before impacting freeman. i took measurements from the drivers side back tire to where the ruts in the grass started and it showed lindley followed freeman off the roadway, in the grass for approximately 241 feet. after 241 feet, lindley accelerated hard approximately 353 from the approximate point of impact as evidenced from the tire mark under and immediately behind the drivers side rear tire. this tire mark differed from the tire marks where lindley was merely following freeman in that the grass had been rubbed off down to the dirt indicating this tire spun at a significant speed just prior to impact. officers had to use an approximate point of impact because freeman was moved back and forth as the vehicle hit him from two different directions. because [roadway] off the roadway and then accelerate just prior to the point of impact, she was arrested for aggravated assault family violence with a deadly weapon. the tire mark evidence shows this was an intentional act of violence against freeman.

records.deidentified_narrative: refer to the mark 43 report with the same case for offense details regarding this crash. unit 1 was parked in a parking spot near building 19. units 2, 3, and 4 were parked a few parking stalls next to unit 1, all of which were parked unoccupied vehicles and parked correctly. unit 5 got out of unit 1 and stood next to unit 1. unit 5 and now unit 1's driver, d1, were involved in a disturbance. d1 entered the driver's seat and abruptly reversed backward. unit 1then proceeded forward but struck unit 5 in the process and knocked him to the ground with the front left of unit 1. unit 1 then continued forward and struck unit 2. the impact caused unit 2 to shift from its parking spot and strike unit 3 and then unit 3 struck unit 4. unit 1's driver, d1 ( and owner), fled the location, failing to stop and provide information or rendering aid to unit 5. both unit 5 and d1 were not at the scene when police arrived. d1 made the scene afterward and spoke with police and then left, unit 5 then made the scene after d1 left and also spoke with police. both unit 5 and d1 advised the other caused the crash and both were intoxicated. unit 5 sustained minor injuries to his right elbow, knees, and shin. ems was requested and evaluated unit 5. coban/bwc available.
